Subject: Acme POC - access provisioning, success criteria, and next steps

Hi Alice 

Thanks for taking the time today  really appreciate the context on Acme's search/QA use case and the evaluation priorities. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned: 

Summary of what we heard
- Goal: 30% reduction in average latency for search-forward generation and parity in relevance vs current in-house LLM.
- Success criteria: P50 latency < 150ms on your baseline, P95 < 350ms; top-3 relevance precision > 85% on the eval set you shared.
- Scope: 2 production-like endpoints (search re-ranker + customer support assistant), ~50k monthly active queries during test window.

POC plan & timeline
- Access + provisioning (this week): API keys, IP allowlist, and SSO invites so your devs can hit the endpoints.
- Eval window (2 weeks): run the provided eval set and a small live A/B against a shadow endpoint.
- Review (after week 2): 30-min sync to review metrics and next steps for Dedicated sizing.

Ownership
- Redwood: provisioning, baseline test harness, and example integration scripts (Marissa).
- Acme: share final eval set, provide IP ranges for allowlist, and confirm SSO users (Alice / Bob).

Immediate asks
1) Please confirm the list of SSO users you want invited (min: 2 devs + 1 security).
2) Share Acme network egress IP ranges so we can add them to the allowlist.
3) If you want the API keys scoped to a team or project, let me know naming.

Attachments: POC_Success_Criteria.xlsx (template)  I’ve attached a starting version you can edit.

If that looks good I’ll send the API key and SSO invites after we get the allowlist.

Thanks  talk soon,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
Attachment: POC_Success_Criteria.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Hi Alice / Bob 

Thanks for the quick replies and the IP ranges  those two CIDRs look good. Answers to your credential questions and next steps below: 

Credentials model
- We provide per-project API keys by default for Dedicated and Hosted evaluations. For this POC I’ll provision two keys: one scoped to "acme-search-poc" (read + generate) and one scoped to "acme-support-poc" (generate + chat). Keys are revocable and we recommend rotating after the POC.
- Short-lived tokens: we support ephemeral tokens via our session API (tokens valid for up to 24 hours) and long-lived API keys for automation. If you want KMS-backed rotation, we can enable it but that takes a bit more setup on both sides (we can iterate after the POC).

Provisioning plan (today/tomorrow)
- Today: I’ll add the two CIDRs to our allowlist and open the SSO invites (you should see Okta invites from redwood.okta.com).
- This afternoon: I’ll create the two scoped API keys and share them in a secure Doc link (access limited to invited users).
- Tomorrow morning: baseline run from Redwood’s test harness against your eval set once keys are in place.

Next steps for you
- Confirm SSO users (Alice / Bob / sec_lead).
- Validate the cleaned eval set when Bob sends it.

Attachments: Network_Allowlist_Instructions.pdf  includes firewall rules and example curl commands.

I’ll follow up once the invites and keys are ready.

Thanks,
